messages:
maya: Quick thread — seeing steady RSS growth on long sessions (~25k tokens) even though token throughput is stable. KV cache reuse rate drops over time, lots of sparsely populated pages.
satoshi: Can you paste the profiler output? which allocator variant are we on for kv pages?
maya: Paste: https://paste.internal/kv-flame-217111 (flame shows lots of alloc/free churn). We use the arena allocator with 4KB pages and 256B subblock rounding. Suspect internal waste from small entries.
lisa: If most entries <100B and we round to 256B that explains the waste. With long contexts this compounds.
niko: We also don't coalesce across pages today — per-page freelists only. That will leave pages at low occupancy.
maya: Correct — no cross-page merge. We're ending up with many pages ~20–30% used.
andrew: What eviction/paging policy do we run? purely LRU?
maya: Age-priority eviction (oldest first). We bias only for huge entries (>1MB). So small old entries stay and keep holes.
satoshi: I ran a quick sim: with 256B granularity fragmentation ratio ~1.7 after ~2M ops. Drop to 64B granularity gives ~1.12 but increases allocation bookkeeping.
lisa: What's the metadata delta for 64B? bitmaps, freelist nodes, etc.
satoshi: Rough calc: bitmap => 1 bit per 64B => ~1/512 = 0.2% mem overhead. But freelist node churn and CPU for alloc/free go up.
maya: Tradeoff: internal waste vs CPU latency. We have p99 SLO headroom of ~5ms; can't break it.
niko: Alternative: background compaction. Scan low-occupancy pages and relocate live entries to compact pages, free others.
andrew: Compaction helps but is heavy. Do it async and throttled; we need relocation-safe handles/indirection.
maya: Good news — we already have an indirection layer handle->physical loc, so relocation is feasible without breaking callers.
lisa: Draft proposal A: change block granularity to 128B, enable cross-page coalesce, and run background compaction for pages <40% occupancy.
satoshi: Proposal B: keep 256B but add per-page hole-score and prefer evicting pages with high hole ratio + age. That reduces migration cost.
niko: Consider hybrid: small-entry arena (64B) for entries <1KB, and large-entry arena for >=1KB so we don't mix sizes on the same page.
maya: Need benchmarks. p99 latency regressions must be <=5ms, throughput loss <=8%. Can infra run microbench traces for 48h?
andrew: I'll queue a perf job using prod-sample-2026-02 trace and baseline vs 128B/64B/hybrid.
deploy-bot: perf-job-317 queued by andrew for trace prod-sample-2026-02. link: https://perf.internal/jobs/317
lisa: :thumbsup: Also we should add telemetry: per-page occupancy histogram, hole-ratio counter, compaction relocations.
maya: I'll open a metrics PR and sketch compaction proto with throttles and backoff heuristics.
satoshi: Note: batching heuristics can help — piggyback compaction work on low-batch windows to avoid interfering with hot request flow.
niko: Also ensure relocation path uses the bulk memcpy kernel and avoids slow generic memcpy; kernel selection matters here for CPU/wall time.
andrew: Ok — action items: maya -> metrics + compaction proto, andrew -> perf job, lisa -> sim metadata cost for 64/128B, niko -> design relocation protocol and coalesce op. We'll reconvene after perf results.
maya: Thanks all. Marking this thread for follow-up in the eng-runtime sync.
